directAnswer: To start a Mac in Safe Mode, hold down the Shift key immediately after turning on or restarting the Mac until you see the login window.
summary: Starting your Mac in Safe Mode can help troubleshoot issues by preventing certain software from loading.

sections.heading: What is Safe Mode?
sections.body: Safe Mode is a diagnostic mode in macOS that starts your Mac with the minimum required software and drivers. It can help isolate issues related to startup items and extensions.

sections.heading: When to Use Safe Mode
sections.body: Use Safe Mode if your Mac is experiencing performance issues, crashes, or if you need to troubleshoot problems with applications or system settings.

steps.title: Shut Down Your Mac
steps.detail: Click on the Apple menu in the top left corner and select 'Shut Down'. Wait for your Mac to completely power off.

steps.title: Power On and Hold Shift
steps.detail: Turn your Mac back on and immediately press and hold the Shift key until you see the login window.

steps.title: Log In
steps.detail: Release the Shift key when you see the login window. You may need to log in twice if FileVault is enabled.

faqs.question: What should I do if my Mac doesn't start in Safe Mode?
faqs.answer: If your Mac doesn't start in Safe Mode, try restarting it and holding the Shift key again. If it still fails, there may be a hardware issue or a problem with your macOS installation.

faqs.question: Can I use all my applications in Safe Mode?
faqs.answer: No, some applications and features may not be available in Safe Mode, as it limits what software runs during startup.

faqs.question: How do I exit Safe Mode?
faqs.answer: To exit Safe Mode, simply restart your Mac without holding any keys during startup.

caveats: Safe Mode may not resolve all issues, and some problems may require further troubleshooting.
